title: A rapid, end-to-end vaccine response to a newly identified pathogen

concept.text: The innovation would be a repeatable response system that moves from recognizing a newly identified pathogen to a vaccine supported by compelling safety and efficacy evidence, appropriately authorized, manufactured at scale and delivered in meaningful quantities to affected populations within the first months. Rapid candidate design is one component; the defining capability is completing the connected clinical, regulatory, manufacturing and delivery chain.

Such a system would combine advance preparation with adaptation during an outbreak. Work on representative pathogens, vaccine libraries, clinical trial readiness, regulatory readiness and manufacturing capacity could shorten the response, while surveillance and public health delivery would connect the vaccine to the populations that need it. Preparation can make stages overlap, but it cannot remove necessary scientific evidence or quality controls.

Scope synthesis: the supplied evidence chiefly concerns responses to viral threats. Repeated success across different viral families would demonstrate broader adaptability than a single deployment, without establishing an ability to produce vaccines against every pathogen. The concept also requires actual substantial delivery, extending beyond the documented 100 Days Mission vaccine milestone of emergency authorization and readiness for production at scale.

significance.text: If effective vaccines reached affected populations early enough, vaccination could begin while an outbreak’s course was still substantially alterable. The revolutionary change would be dependable access to protection during the initial response, rather than speed confined to laboratory design or trial initiation. The reports’ rationale connects rapid access to safe, effective countermeasures with the possibility of changing pandemic trajectories.

Conditional impact synthesis: earlier protection could reduce severe illness and deaths and, where the vaccine also reduces infection or infectiousness, help suppress transmission. Downstream possibilities include less pressure on health services and less social and economic disruption. Those effects would depend on outbreak dynamics, vaccine performance, the time needed to develop immunity, uptake and whether delivery reaches people at risk.

A reusable vaccine platform should not be understood as a guarantee of a predictable response to every new virus. Protective immunity can differ between pathogens, and clinical testing, regulatory assessment, manufacturing and access remain linked constraints. Even a successful rapid-response system would not guarantee containment of every outbreak; an authorized product that cannot be manufactured and delivered promptly would provide only part of the intended benefit.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is reliable integration of the entire response under outbreak conditions across substantially different viral threats. Fast performance in one stage does not establish that evidence generation, authorization, production and delivery can all finish within the same early-response window. The January 2026 implementation report identifies continuing gaps and explains that the required capacities must work together.

A central scientific barrier is determining what immune response actually protects against a newly identified pathogen. Conventional clinical-endpoint efficacy trials require sufficient disease incidence and follow-up to distinguish protection from chance. Validated immune markers, including accepted correlates of protection, or other appropriate regulatory pathways may sometimes support evaluation when conventional endpoints are infeasible. However, few correlates are widely accepted, and an immune response cannot automatically be treated as proof of clinical protection.

The engineering and organizational barriers include ready clinical trial networks, coordinated regulatory review, manufacturing capacity that can produce the relevant vaccine at scale, and supply and distribution arrangements that translate production into access. Clinical development, manufacturing preparation, regulatory work and distribution planning need to overlap while respecting their dependencies. Acceleration must preserve standards for quality, safety and efficacy.

current_state.text: CEPI’s 2024 Annual Progress Report documents a concrete rapid-response achievement during Rwanda’s 2024 Marburg outbreak: an investigational vaccine entered a CEPI-supported, open-label Phase 2 trial on 5 October 2024, ten days after the outbreak was declared, with frontline health workers beginning to receive it. This demonstrates rapid trial deployment. It does not establish that a vaccine was newly designed, shown to be efficacious, authorized, manufactured at population scale and substantially delivered within those ten days.

The same report describes enabling work on vaccine libraries, regulatory readiness and response exercises. These are meaningful preparations for faster responses. Exercises can test decision-making, engagement and response mechanisms and reveal gaps, but they do not demonstrate a vaccine’s clinical effectiveness.

The 100 Days Mission Implementation Report 2026, dated 27 January 2026, describes the 100-day target as still unachievable in many areas. Its vaccine milestone is emergency use authorization and readiness for production at scale. The supplied evidence therefore documents both progress and continuing gaps at that date; it does not demonstrate the broader capability proposed here, which additionally requires substantial delivery.

Evidence coverage is limited to the supplied review of partial extracts from these reports. Both extracts were truncated and carried warnings that some PDF pages lacked extractable text; the CEPI extract ended during page 50 and the implementation-report extract during page 42. The supplied review nevertheless identifies text supporting the Rwanda milestone and the January 2026 assessment. No freshness search record establishes developments through 1 November 2026 or later, so these dated findings should not be presented as a complete late-2026 account. These limitations do not invalidate the historical results supported by the available passages.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: complete multiple prospectively defined outbreak responses involving different viral families. In each response, produce compelling safety and efficacy evidence through an appropriate evidentiary pathway, obtain appropriate authorization, manufacture at scale and deliver meaningful quantities to affected populations within a prespecified early-response window. Repetition would test whether the integrated system works beyond a single favorable deployment.
completion_criteria.label: Repeat complete vaccine responses across viral families within prespecified windows

completion_criteria.text: Proposed measurement requirements: before each response, define the clock’s starting event, the deadline, acceptable evidence, manufacturing quantities, delivery quantities, target populations and intended coverage. Report the timing and outcome of each stage separately so that rapid candidate generation or trial initiation cannot stand in for completed delivery. These are proposed assessment criteria, not established numerical standards.
completion_criteria.label: Predefine response criteria and report each stage’s timing and outcome

completion_criteria.text: The proposed delivery requirement deliberately exceeds the documented 100 Days Mission milestone of emergency authorization and readiness for production at scale. Readiness exercises would provide complementary evidence about coordination and preparedness; clinical effectiveness would still require appropriate clinical evidence rather than rehearsal results.
completion_criteria.label: Demonstrate actual vaccine delivery with appropriate clinical effectiveness evidence

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and boundary assessment: document successful and unsuccessful responses, make evidence sufficiently transparent for independent assessment, and repeat demonstrations across differing viral families and operational settings. State the demonstrated limits, including where prior pathogen knowledge, accepted immune markers or existing manufacturing capacity were necessary. Finite tests would establish demonstrated breadth, not literal universality, and would not justify relaxing safety or evidence requirements for subsequent responses.
completion_criteria.label: Report independently assessable response outcomes and demonstrated applicability limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: INF-08, “A pre-emptive vaccine against diverse pandemic coronaviruses,” overlaps most directly through vaccine preparedness. INF-08 seeks protection across diverse coronaviruses before a particular threat emerges; INF-09 seeks a rapid response after a new threat is recognized, with repeatability across viral families. Either could benefit the other, but preparedness through breadth and preparedness through response speed remain distinct goals.

Roster-based synthesis: INF-01, “A broadly protective HIV vaccine,” INF-03, “A tuberculosis vaccine that interrupts transmission,” and INF-13, “A highly protective, durable and readily deliverable malaria vaccine,” share requirements for protective immunity, clinical evidence and practical delivery. Their defining advances concern particular pathogens and protection goals. INF-09 concerns the speed and reliability of an integrated response and does not itself solve their pathogen-specific immunological challenges.

Roster-based synthesis: INF-05, “Near-patient diagnosis of the cause and treatability of most serious infections,” could complement threat recognition and clinical response, while INF-07, “Broad-spectrum treatment for unrelated viral infections,” could offer treatment during vaccine development. Diagnosis, treatment and vaccination have different endpoints; success in one would not demonstrate completion of the others.

Roster-based synthesis: INF-06, “A dependable platform for generating new antibacterial treatments,” and INF-15, “A rapidly adaptable clinical phage-therapy platform,” share the ambition of repeatable development rather than isolated product success. They target bacterial treatment through different modalities, whereas INF-09 targets preventive vaccination and an outbreak response extending through population delivery.

Roster-based synthesis: INF-02, “A safe, scalable cure for established HIV infection,” INF-11, “A safe, broadly effective treatment-free cure for chronic hepatitis B,” and INF-12, “Very short, reliable curative treatment for active and latent tuberculosis,” concern curing established infection. Their evidence, manufacturing and access challenges overlap operationally with INF-09, but preventive vaccine deployment does not establish eradication of an existing infection.

Roster-based synthesis: INF-04, “A reliable way to break malaria transmission through its vectors,” intervenes through vectors rather than vaccination. INF-10, “Prevention of multiple sclerosis by controlling Epstein–Barr virus,” and INF-14, “Mechanism-guided prevention of major post-viral syndromes,” focus on downstream disease prevention. Rapid vaccine delivery might complement these goals where relevant, but it would not by itself establish vector control or prevention of those later outcomes.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish developments after the report dated 27 January 2026 or a complete state of the field through 1 November 2026 or later.
Both report extracts are truncated and have extraction warnings. Material outside the reviewed passages remains unassessed.

The earlier claim that a web tool rejected the 2026 PDF because of its size cannot be verified from the supplied artifacts. It was omitted from the reader-facing account because it does not accurately describe the evidence available in the supplied review.
The response clock’s starting event, early-response window, evidence thresholds, manufacturing and delivery quantities, and target coverage remain to be specified.
The extent to which accepted immune markers or alternative regulatory pathways would be available for a particular newly identified pathogen remains pathogen-dependent.
The supplied evidence principally addresses viral threats; applicability to newly identified nonviral pathogens is not established.
The supplied Rwanda milestone does not resolve whether or when that response completed the full chain of efficacy evidence, authorization, scaled manufacturing and substantial delivery.

brief.title: Vaccines that reach people early in a new outbreak
possible: People facing a newly identified disease could receive a vaccine within the first months of an outbreak. It would have strong evidence of safety and protection, authorization for use, and enough doses manufactured and delivered to reach affected populations.
A prepared response system would connect testing, approval, production and delivery. It would work repeatedly across different families of viruses.
why: Earlier protection could prevent severe illness and deaths while an outbreak’s course can still be changed. People at risk would gain protection during the initial response.
Fewer people becoming seriously ill could ease pressure on health services and reduce disruption to everyday life and the economy.

sources.not_established: Authorization and production readiness do not establish that enough vaccine doses actually reach affected populations.

shown: In Rwanda, a CEPI-supported trial began giving an experimental Marburg vaccine to frontline health workers 10 days after the outbreak was declared. This demonstrated rapid trial deployment; it did not demonstrate completion of the full response.

CEPI has also advanced vaccine libraries, collections of candidates prepared for related viruses, alongside manufacturing networks and regulatory preparation. These provide parts of a faster response.
missing: Repeated responses must connect evidence, authorization, large-scale manufacturing and substantial delivery within the same early window.
Researchers still need reliable ways to establish protection against a new virus when too few cases occur for conventional trials.
Trial networks, regulators, factories and distribution systems must work together fast enough to reach people at risk.

milestones.label: Complete rapid responses across different virus families
milestones.explanation: Repeated outbreaks across different virus families would have to yield strong safety and protection evidence, authorization, scaled production and substantial delivery within preset windows. This would establish repeatability.

milestones.label: Define success beforehand and measure every stage
milestones.explanation: Each response would need advance definitions of its start, deadline, evidence, production, delivery and population coverage, followed by results for every stage. This would make completion measurable.

milestones.label: Deliver vaccines with clinical evidence of protection
milestones.explanation: Vaccines would have to reach affected populations with appropriate clinical evidence that they protect people. This would establish the benefit beyond approval, production readiness or response rehearsals.

milestones.label: Make outcomes and limits independently assessable
milestones.explanation: Successes and failures across virus families and settings would need independently assessable evidence, including dependencies on prior knowledge and capacity. This would establish the system’s demonstrated reach and limits.

uncertain: The starting event, deadline, evidence thresholds, dose quantities and population coverage needed to count as success remain undefined.
It remains unclear which new viruses could be assessed using immune markers, measurable immune responses known to predict protection.
Success across several virus families would not establish that the system works against every virus or against nonviral causes of disease.

page.title: Rapid pandemic vaccine development and deployment
page.definition: Within 100 days of recognizing a new pandemic threat, a safe and effective vaccine is ready for initial authorization and large-scale manufacture. Deployment extends through production of complete vaccine courses, equitable allocation and vaccination of people at risk in the quantities needed to control the outbreak.

goal.need: By 29 November 2020, countries had reported over 1.4 million COVID-19 deaths. While people wait for vaccines, communities rely on measures such as isolation and distancing. A model estimated that starting each country’s vaccinations 232 days earlier, with the same rollout pattern and public health measures, could have averted 8.33 million deaths by the end of 2021 (95% credible interval 7.70–8.68 million), mostly in lower-middle-income countries. The model excluded China. Saving that time depends on how soon doses reach people.

figures.caption: Modelled COVID-19 deaths averted by the end of 2021
figures.note: Low- and middle-income countries are included in the global total. Estimates are those summarized by CEPI.

statements.quote: Rapidly make and equitably deploy safe and effective vaccines
statements.context: The objective introducing section 3.4, Vaccines, of the National Biodefense Strategy and Implementation Plan.

statements.quote: An effective rapid response depends on the whole chain, from detection and scientific understanding to development, testing, approval, production and delivery.
Vaccines ready to be produced at scale for global deployment.
statements.context: The partnership’s report to the G7 set a 100-day target from WHO’s declaration of a public health emergency of international concern.

statements.quote: the 100-day target is not yet achievable in many areas.
statements.context: The fifth implementation report identifies gaps in diagnostics, therapeutics, vaccines and the systems that deliver them.

completion.title: A U.S. outbreak response meets the 100-day review, 130-day production and 100-day administration targets.
completion.criterion: For a human viral threat with a developed vaccine candidate, complete design, testing and review of a safe and effective vaccine within 100 days of determining that a potentially nationally or internationally significant biological incident exists. Within 130 days of that determination, produce enough complete courses to vaccinate the U.S. population. Within 100 days of authorization or approval, safely, securely and equitably allocate and administer to people at risk the quantity needed to control the incident.
completion.set_by: United States Government, National Biodefense Strategy and Implementation Plan, sections 3.4.1, 3.4.2 and 3.4.4; domestic human-vaccine targets.
completion.threshold_quote: within one hundred days following authorization or approval.
completion.basis: The U.S. strategy sets domestic capability targets. Meeting all three in the same response would demonstrate that capability for the threat involved. Production is measured against the U.S. population. Administration is measured against the at-risk population and the needs of the incident. CEPI measures readiness for initial authorization from threat identification.

milestones.title: A vaccine candidate induces antibody or cellular responses in an appropriate animal model.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate a vaccine-induced antibody or cellular immune response in an appropriate animal model, with product characterization and safety evidence supporting clinical development. The required nonclinical studies depend on the vaccine and its intended use.
milestones.set_by: WHO Expert Committee on Biological Standardization, WHO guidelines on nonclinical evaluation of vaccines, section 3 and the definition of preclinical evaluation.
milestones.threshold_quote: Immunization studies in animal models should be conducted because they may provide valuable “proof of concept” information to support a clinical development plan.

milestones.title: An outbreak vaccine is administered to people under a regulator-permitted clinical investigation.
milestones.criterion: Give the candidate vaccine to a participant in a clinical investigation permitted by the regulator after review of the preclinical evidence, manufacturing information, product quality and safety.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Vaccine Development – 101, clinical-development stage and Investigational New Drug application assessment.
milestones.threshold_quote: reasonably safe for testing of the vaccine to move forward in people.

milestones.title: A vaccine’s Phase 2 results support selection of a dose and formulation for pivotal testing.
milestones.criterion: Obtain controlled Phase 2 data on safety and on the relationship between dose and immune response sufficient to select one or more formulations for pivotal testing.
milestones.set_by: WHO Expert Committee on Biological Standardization, Guidelines on clinical evaluation of vaccines, section 4.2.1, and FDA, Vaccine Development – 101, Phase 2.
milestones.threshold_quote: immunogenicity data to support the selection of one or more candidate formulations for evaluation in pivotal trials

milestones.title: A vaccine meets its agreed pivotal efficacy or immune-response endpoint.
milestones.criterion: Against a group unvaccinated against the target disease, the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval for efficacy must exceed a prespecified positive threshold chosen for clinical importance. Against a vaccine of demonstrated efficacy, a non-inferiority trial must meet its prespecified, justified margin. Where protection can be inferred from an established immune correlate, meet the agreed endpoint for that immune response.
milestones.set_by: WHO Expert Committee on Biological Standardization, Guidelines on clinical evaluation of vaccines: regulatory expectations, sections 6.3.9.3 and 6.1.1.
milestones.threshold_quote: the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval around the estimate of vaccine efficacy is above a predefined percentage

milestones.title: A new-virus vaccine is ready for initial authorization and manufacturing at scale within 100 days.
milestones.criterion: Within 100 days of identifying a new pandemic threat, a safe and effective vaccine is ready for initial authorization and for manufacture at scale.
milestones.set_by: 100 Days Mission, using CEPI’s published definition of the G7/G20-backed programme; the clock starts at threat identification.
milestones.threshold_quote: CEPI’s 100 Days Mission aims to develop safe, effective and accessible vaccines within 100 days of identifying a new pandemic threat.

milestones.title: A new-virus vaccine is produced for the U.S. population within 130 days.
milestones.criterion: Produce enough complete courses of safe and effective vaccine to vaccinate the U.S. population within 130 days of the determination of a potential nationally or internationally significant biological incident. Count courses according to the number of doses required per person.
milestones.set_by: United States Government, National Biodefense Strategy and Implementation Plan, section 3.4.2, domestic vaccine-production target.

milestones.title: FDA authorizes or approves the vaccine for use in the outbreak.
milestones.criterion: FDA issues an emergency use authorization or approves the vaccine for the outbreak indication. Use the date of that decision as the start of the domestic administration period.
milestones.set_by: United States Government, National Biodefense Strategy and Implementation Plan, section 3.4.4, and U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Vaccine Development – 101.

milestones.title: Vaccine reaches the administration sites designated for the outbreak within product specifications.
milestones.criterion: Apportion and transport vaccine to receiving sites according to incident needs, including the sites designated to administer it. Maintain product integrity during transport and distribution according to safety requirements and manufacturer specifications.
milestones.set_by: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Public Health Emergency Preparedness and Response Capabilities, capability 9, function 3, tasks 1 and 2.
milestones.threshold_quote: Maintain medical materiel integrity in accordance with established safety and manufacturer specifications during transport and distribution.

not_found: No documented outbreak response meeting all three linked U.S. timing targets was located.
The CEPI, G7 and U.S. strategy documents examined did not yield a required number of successful responses across viral families.

results.finding: mRNA-1273 elicited a live-virus neutralization geometric mean titer of 3481 in the high-dose rhesus macaque group (n=8).
results.detail: The reported safety evidence addresses vaccine-associated lung immunopathology after challenge.
results.quote: geometric mean titers of 501 in the 10-μg dose group and 3481 in the 100-μg dose group.

results.finding: All 45 Phase 1 participants received mRNA-1273, with the first vaccination 66 days after the viral genome sequence was posted.
results.quote: The 45 enrolled participants received their first vaccination between March 16 and April 14, 2020 (Fig. S1).

results.finding: In 45 Phase 1 participants, mRNA-1273 at 100 μg elicited strong neutralization with better tolerability than the highest dose.
results.detail: The trial had no placebo arm. The planned pivotal dose was reported as an expectation.
results.quote: Of the three doses evaluated, the 100-μg dose elicits high neutralization responses and Th1-skewed CD4 T cell responses, coupled with a reactogenicity profile that is more favorable than that of the higher dose.

results.finding: mRNA-1273 was administered in a regulator-approved Phase 2 trial with 600 randomized adults.
results.quote: The mRNA-1273 vaccine and placebo were administered as a deltoid intramuscular injection using a 2-dose regimen with the first dose given on day 1 and the second on day 29.

results.finding: In the mRNA-1273 Phase 2 trial (600 randomized), 100% of vaccine recipients tested on day 43 seroconverted.
results.detail: The trial compared 50 and 100 µg given 28 days apart. Solicited reactions were mostly mild or moderate, and the preliminary analysis covered safety and immunogenicity through day 57.
results.quote: By day 43, 14 days after the second vaccination, seroconversion rates of 100% were observed for all participants tested in both cohorts.

results.finding: In COVE, 14,635 of 15,209 participants assigned to mRNA-1273 received a second injection.
results.quote: More than 96% of participants (14,727 in the placebo group and 14,635 in the mRNA-1273 group) received second injections.

results.finding: In the 28,451-participant per-protocol analysis, mRNA-1273 had a 95% confidence interval lower bound of 91.0% for efficacy against symptomatic COVID-19.
results.quote: Vaccine efficacy in preventing Covid-19 illness was 93.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 91.0 to 94.8), with 55 confirmed cases in the mRNA-1273 group (9.6 per 1000 person-years; 95% CI, 7.2 to 12.5) and 744 in the placebo group (136.6 per 1000 person-years; 95% CI, 127.0 to 146.8).

results.finding: Experimental Bundibugyo vaccines were first given to Phase 1 participants 80 days after the first reported DRC case (participant count unreported).
results.quote: Researchers dosed the first participants in Phase 1 trials of experimental vaccines 80 days after the first Bundibugyo case was reported in the DRC.

results.finding: At day 100 after the emergency declaration, the Bundibugyo vaccine portfolio had no approved vaccine (participant count unreported).
results.detail: The source’s 100-day clock starts at the emergency declaration. The criterion starts at threat identification. Approval status alone does not establish whether a candidate was ready for authorization.
results.quote: Still, at the 100-day mark, there is no approved vaccine specifically against Bundibugyo virus.

results.finding: CDC recorded initial COVID-19 vaccinations for 40,517,900 people during the first two months of the U.S. rollout.
results.detail: The sample counts vaccine recipients. The report does not enumerate administration sites or provide shipment or temperature records.
results.quote: During December 14, 2020−February 14, 2021, a total of 40,517,900 persons initiated the COVID-19 vaccination series and had vaccine administration data reported to CDC by February 20, 2021.

results.finding: The first 800,000 doses of the MHRA-authorised Pfizer/BioNTech SARS-CoV-2 vaccine completed batch safety testing.
results.detail: The 40 million doses were pre-orders for future delivery. The speech gives no vaccine-specific clinical trial sample size.
results.quote: I can confirm that batch testing has been completed this morning for the first deployment of 800,000 doses of the vaccine.

results.finding: Of the two COVID-19 vaccine EUAs reported, the earlier was for Pfizer-BioNTech on December 11, 2020.
results.quote:
On December 11, 2020, FDA issued an EUA to Pfizer, 
Inc. for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine, subject to the terms of 
the Authorization.

results.finding: The U.S. COVID-19 vaccination program shipped vaccine to over 107,500 unique locations by the end of the public health emergency.
results.detail: The location count measures shipping reach. En-route monitoring was available for Pfizer-BioNTech shipments, but the paper provides no count or rate of shipments received within required temperature limits.
results.quote: vaccine was shipped to over 107,500 unique locations by the end of the COVID-19 public health emergency declaration on May 11, 2023.

results.finding: In Michigan, 21 Moderna COVID-19 vaccine shipments were affected by temperatures below the permitted range in transit.
results.detail: The release gives no total shipment count for the distribution period.
results.quote: 21 shipments of safe and effective COVID-19 vaccine impacted due to temperature issues during shipment by distributor

results.finding: Single-dose ChAd3-MARV induced a protective immune response in nonhuman primates (n unreported) within 7 days.
results.detail: The 7-day figure measures time to protective immunity. The excerpt reports antigen-specific antibodies as a correlate of protection and gives no antibody concentration.
results.quote: Protective immunity was achieved within 7 days of vaccination and was maintained through 1 year after vaccination. Antigen-specific antibodies were an immune correlate of protection in the acute challenge model, and their concentration was predictive of protection.

results.finding: In Rwanda’s Marburg outbreak, 1,710 frontline workers and high-risk contacts received ChAd3-MARV after emergency authorization.
results.detail: The first emergency vaccination preceded the first phase 2 enrollment by five days. The article reports prior phase 1 safety evidence, but leaves the basis of the regulator’s authorization unspecified.
results.quote:
In addition, 1710 frontline 
workers and high-risk contacts received the chimpanzee adenovirus 3–vectored vac-
cine ChAd3-MARV under emergency use authorization in a phase 2 clinical trial.

results.finding: In a Phase 1 trial of cAd3-Marburg in 40 adults, 95% in each dose group developed a Marburg glycoprotein-specific antibody response by week 4.
results.detail: Participants entered the two dose groups sequentially. The trial had no placebo group and was sized primarily for safety.
results.quote: In both groups, 95% of participants responded to the vaccine at four weeks after vaccination as determined by a significant increase in Marburg GP-specific antibody titers over baseline

results.finding: Investigational Marburg vaccination began 10 days after Rwanda declared the outbreak. Trial sample size was unreported.
results.detail: National ethics and regulatory committees approved the Phase 2 trial protocol for frontline workers. Shipment totals measure doses delivered and do not establish manufacturing capacity.
results.quote: 10 Days From Marburg Outbreak Declaration to Vaccination: A High-Level Timeline

results.finding: Sabin’s investigational Marburg vaccine had 7,000 finished doses in stock.
results.detail: The reported quantity counts doses. The report gives no complete-course count for that stock or elapsed production time from a qualifying incident determination.
results.quote: 7000 doses of drug product in stock.

results.finding: Rwanda’s Phase 2 Marburg outbreak trial delivered investigational vaccine to clinics, with more than 1,700 priority recipients vaccinated by the end of October 2024.
results.detail: The recipient count shows that vaccine reached administration sites. The report describes packaging and labeling for import, while evidence of cold-chain conditions or product integrity at receipt is absent.
results.quote:
The trial began the following day,
once all GCP components were in place, and by the end of October 2024,
over 1700 frontline and healthcare workers and high-risk contacts had
received the investigational vaccine and were being monitored.

results.finding: In 11 ERVEBO-vaccinated ferrets, the geometric mean endpoint IgG titer against Bundibugyo virus glycoprotein was 16,582.
results.detail: One of 12 vaccinated ferrets had insufficient serum for Bundibugyo testing. The assay measured antibody binding.
results.quote:
At 
16,582, the geometric mean endpoint titer for BDBV 
glycoprotein-specific IgG was significantly lower 
than that for EBOV glycoprotein (Wilcoxon statistical 
test = 3; p = 1.6 × 10–4), despite limited overlap in the 
range of titers, which extended from 3,200 to 30,270.

results.finding: ChAdOx1 BDBV Phase 1 trial: 1 volunteer reported vaccinated.
results.detail: Confirmation applies to the first vaccination reported by the Health Research Authority. Total trial enrollment is unstated.
results.quote:
The first volunteer in a
world-first clinical trial of a vaccine
designed to protect against Bundibugyo Ebolavirus (BDBV) has been successfully vaccinated.

results.finding: UNICEF supported deployment of 68,920 ERVEBO doses during the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
results.detail: The dose count covers deployment. Site-level shipment and receipt records and cold-chain monitoring results are absent.
results.quote:
UNICEF supported
the deployment of 68,920 ERVEBO doses, vaccine stock
management and cold-chain strengthening.

case_label = "Virus". Reason: The readiness scorecard and vaccine studies distinguish the virus against which each candidate is evaluated.

definition = "Within 100 days of recognizing a new pandemic threat, a safe and effective vaccine is ready for initial authorization and large-scale manufacture. Deployment extends through production of complete vaccine courses, equitable allocation and vaccination of people at risk in the quantities needed to control the outbreak.". Reason: The definition leaves the 100-day starting event implicit and omits manufacturing readiness from the day-100 objective.

goal.need = "By 29 November 2020, countries had reported over 1.4 million COVID-19 deaths. While people wait for vaccines, communities rely on measures such as isolation and distancing. A model estimated that starting each country\u2019s vaccinations 232 days earlier, with the same rollout pattern and public health measures, could have averted 8.33 million deaths by the end of 2021 (95% credible interval 7.70\u20138.68 million), mostly in lower-middle-income countries. The model excluded China. Saving that time depends on how soon doses reach people.". Reason: The current text refers to missing mortality estimates and omits the difference between earlier authorization and earlier vaccination in the model.

add statement by Pandemic Preparedness Partnership, 2021: "Vaccines ready to be produced at scale for global deployment.". Reason: The founding report identifies both the international vaccine goal and the event that started its proposed clock.

add statement by International Pandemic Preparedness Secretariat, 2026: "the 100-day target is not yet achievable in many areas.". Reason: The implementation body’s assessment records the limits of present readiness alongside the programme’s stated ambition.

edit completion: title = "A U.S. outbreak response meets the 100-day review, 130-day production and 100-day administration targets."; criterion = "For a human viral threat with a developed vaccine candidate, complete design, testing and review of a safe and effective vaccine within 100 days of determining that a potentially nationally or internationally significant biological incident exists. Within 130 days of that determination, produce enough complete courses to vaccinate the U.S. population. Within 100 days of authorization or approval, safely, securely and equitably allocate and administer to people at risk the quantity needed to control the incident."; threshold_quote = "within one hundred days following authorization or approval."; threshold_ref = 2; basis = "The U.S. strategy sets domestic capability targets. Meeting all three in the same response would demonstrate that capability for the threat involved. Production is measured against the U.S. population. Administration is measured against the at-risk population and the needs of the incident. CEPI measures readiness for initial authorization from threat identification."; refs = [2, 4]. Reason: The title mentions only administration, and the basis needs to distinguish the strategy’s capacity targets from their demonstration in an outbreak.
add case "SARS-CoV-2". Reason: The mRNA-1273 animal and pivotal clinical studies tested protection against SARS-CoV-2.
add case "Marburg virus". Reason: The Rwanda outbreak supplied virus-specific evidence of rapid deployment of an investigational Marburg vaccine.
add case "Bundibugyo virus". Reason: The 2026 Bundibugyo response has its own clinical and production evidence, and protection from the licensed Ebola vaccine remains uncertain for this virus.

edit m1: criterion = "Demonstrate a vaccine-induced antibody or cellular immune response in an appropriate animal model, with product characterization and safety evidence supporting clinical development. The required nonclinical studies depend on the vaccine and its intended use.". Reason: The macaque study’s group sizes and observations are results rather than requirements of WHO’s nonclinical test.

edit m2: criterion = "Give the candidate vaccine to a participant in a clinical investigation permitted by the regulator after review of the preclinical evidence, manufacturing information, product quality and safety.". Reason: The COVID-19 trial’s date, doses and enrollment obscure the event that counts as first administration in humans.

edit m3: criterion = "Obtain controlled Phase 2 data on safety and on the relationship between dose and immune response sufficient to select one or more formulations for pivotal testing."; set_by = "WHO Expert Committee on Biological Standardization, Guidelines on clinical evaluation of vaccines, section 4.2.1, and FDA, Vaccine Development \u2013 101, Phase 2."; set_by_kind = "standards_body"; threshold_quote = "immunogenicity data to support the selection of one or more candidate formulations for evaluation in pivotal trials"; threshold_ref = 9. Reason: WHO defines this stage by evidence supporting formulation selection, while the existing criterion also counts trial enrollment and reports a study-specific antibody cutoff.

edit m4: criterion = "Against a group unvaccinated against the target disease, the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval for efficacy must exceed a prespecified positive threshold chosen for clinical importance. Against a vaccine of demonstrated efficacy, a non-inferiority trial must meet its prespecified, justified margin. Where protection can be inferred from an established immune correlate, meet the agreed endpoint for that immune response."; threshold_quote = "the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval around the estimate of vaccine efficacy is above a predefined percentage"; threshold_ref = 9. Reason: The pivotal test needs WHO’s active-control option and should not present the COVE trial’s numerical result as part of the threshold.

edit m5: criterion = "Within 100 days of identifying a new pandemic threat, a safe and effective vaccine is ready for initial authorization and for manufacture at scale.". Reason: The Bundibugyo portfolio and approval status are dated observations, while CEPI’s milestone tests readiness for a decision and for manufacture.

add milestone after m5: "FDA authorizes or approves the vaccine for use in the outbreak.". Reason: The regulatory decision that starts the domestic administration clock is missing between readiness for review and deployment.

edit m6: criterion = "Produce enough complete courses of safe and effective vaccine to vaccinate the U.S. population within 130 days of the determination of a potential nationally or internationally significant biological incident. Count courses according to the number of doses required per person.". Reason: The production criterion should name its own starting event and measure complete regimens independently of the reported number of investigational doses.

add milestone after m6: "Vaccine reaches the administration sites designated for the outbreak within product specifications.". Reason: The existing milestones end at production and omit delivery of usable vaccine to the sites where people can receive it.
remove not found 2. Reason: The Medicines Patent Pool copy of the January 2026 IPPS implementation report is accessible, including its scorecard and methodology.
